title: Find out why the editor window sometimes runs away to 100000 points wide as a video opens, and crashes
goal: About one walk in fifty, the loop's test copy of the app crashes as a short screen recording opens: the editor window grows to about 100000 points wide, the layout never settles and AppKit stops the app. Find what makes the window grow, whether a person opening a video could hit it, and fix it.

2026-11-19 runner (third look), reproduced and the message captured:
* The exception, captured by the probe's new recorder: NSGenericException "The window has been marked as needing another Update Constraints in Window pass, but it has already had more Update Constraints in Window passes than there are views in the window. <SwiftUI.AppKitWindow> {{40, 56}, {100966, 1028}}". Recorded twice (16:41 and 16:50, ~/Library/Logs/Photonz Probe/exceptions.jsonl).
* Both times the window was already 100000x1028 at the walk's open step (asked for 1440x900); 1028 is the screen's usable height, so AppKit clamped the height and not the width. contentMinSize stayed 480x432, so it is NOT SwiftUI's minimum size pushing the window. The hosting view inside was 100288x1118 (canvas 100023x830, inspector beside it, the timeline pushed below the bottom at y 1118). Nothing in Sources sets a 100000 frame (EditorState.sizeWindowToImageIfReady clamps to the screen unless contentMinSize is huge; VideoWindowLayout clamps; no windowResizability/defaultSize anywhere).
* Rate: scrub-never-blacks-out-walk 28 runs, 0 crashes. sound-effects-eq-compressor-locked-walk: 0 in 25, then 1 in a 23-walk batch (Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build sound, 17th walk), then 1 on the first launch after a probe rebuild, then 0 in 44 more (7 of those under 10 bounded CPU burners). So about 2 in 100, at the open of a video, not about scrubbing.
* Ruled out in a stand-alone app: an infinite SwiftUI minimum gives a different AppKit exception (NaN/inf frame); a huge finite minimum just grows the window with no crash; an ideal width chasing its own width does not grow a plain NSHostingView window. The editor's root .frame(minWidth:minHeight:) also hides inner minimums from contentMinSize.
* Next step: the probe now writes, once per process, the call stack of the first resize that makes any window wider than four screens (kind runawayWindow in the same file), and Scripts/crash-report.mjs prints it under the exception. The next crash (crash-watch, or a batch of sound walks) names the call that grows the window; fix that.
* Command: Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build sound (or the locked EQ walk in a loop), then node Scripts/crash-report.mjs --file <the .ips>.
acceptance: The scrub walk on the long edit (Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/scrub-never-blacks-out-walk.json) is run at least 20 times on a probe built from main, and crash-watch is read after: the count of crashes is written in the log
